title: Drift Wood #26 · the dumpster
logline: A December night behind the bowling alley. Nothing tied there yet. The strip goes and looks anyway.

panels.composition: SMALL WOOD LANES at night from across 101. All the letters lit. WOOD and GULLY crossing the lot.

balloons.text: League night. Uncle's short a man.
I don't bowl. I observe bowling.

image.prompt: a small-town bowling alley at night from across the highway, its neon sign fully lit, two teenagers crossing the parking lot, one with a bowling bag, black and white with heavy blacks

panels.composition: Behind the alley, the shortcut. A rusted dumpster. Chain-link. WOOD stops.

balloons.text: Nothing. It's just a very complete dumpster.

image.prompt: two teenagers behind a bowling alley at night, one stopped and looking at a rusted dumpster beside a chain-link fence under a bare bulb

panels.composition: Wood drawing it on the spot, pad against the fence. The dumpster, the chain, the bulb.

image.prompt: close-up of a teenage boy drawing a rusted dumpster on a pad braced against a chain-link fence at night under a bare bulb

panels.composition: Inside, later: the lanes. Gully bowling. Wood in the plastic seats, still drawing the dumpster from memory. Nobody is tied to anything yet.

image.prompt: inside a bowling alley, a boy in a backwards cap bowling in the middle distance while a boy in an overcoat sits in the plastic seats drawing, black and white, no words

notes: The place, a year before the dog. The strip doesn't know why it went to look.
